title: Partial Fractions
summary: A proper rational function splits into a sum of simpler fractions whose denominators are the factors of the original. Each piece integrates to a logarithm or arctangent, making $\int\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\,dx$ tractable.

partial fractions.plain: Breaking one fraction into a sum of simpler ones.
partial fractions.in_class: Match denominators to the factors of $Q(x)$.

proper fraction.plain: Numerator degree less than denominator degree.
proper fraction.in_class: Required first; otherwise do polynomial division.

repeated factor.plain: A factor raised to a power, $(x-a)^2$.

irreducible quadratic.plain: A quadratic with no real roots.

cover-up method.plain: Fast way to find constants over linear factors.
cover-up method.in_class: Plug in the factor's root to isolate that constant.

clear denominators.plain: Multiply through to solve for the constants.
clear denominators.in_class: Then match coefficients or substitute roots.

concept_sections.heading: Set up the decomposition
concept_sections.explanation: Factor $Q(x)$ fully. Each distinct linear factor $(x-a)$ gives $\dfrac{A}{x-a}$; repeated factors give a term per power; irreducible quadratics give $\dfrac{Ax+B}{\ldots}$.
math_steps: Write one fraction per factor (per power for repeats).

concept_sections.heading: Solve for the constants
concept_sections.explanation: Clear denominators and either substitute the roots (cover-up) or match coefficients of like powers to get a system for $A,B,\ldots$.
math_steps: Plug in roots to isolate constants, or equate coefficients.

concept_sections.heading: Improper fractions first
concept_sections.explanation: If the numerator's degree is $\ge$ the denominator's, do polynomial long division first: write quotient plus a proper remainder, then decompose the remainder.
math_steps: Divide to get quotient + proper fraction.

concept_sections.heading: Integrating the pieces
concept_sections.explanation: Each simple fraction integrates cleanly: $\int\dfrac{A}{x-a}\,dx=A\ln|x-a|$, and $\dfrac{Ax+B}{x^2+c}$ splits into a log and an arctangent.
math_steps: Split quadratic terms into log + arctan.

concept_sections.heading: Repeated and quadratic factors
concept_sections.explanation: Repeated linear factors and irreducible quadratics need their full set of terms; missing a term makes the system unsolvable. Include every power and every $Ax+B$.

real_world_examples.title: Logistic population model
real_world_examples.scenario: Growth that slows as it nears a cap.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Solving it requires $\int\frac{dP}{P(1-P)}$, a partial-fraction integral.

real_world_examples.title: Circuit charge over time
real_world_examples.scenario: A rational rate expression in an RC network.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Partial fractions integrate the rational function to describe the charge.

real_world_examples.title: Chemical reaction rates
real_world_examples.scenario: Concentration change as a ratio of polynomials.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Rate laws often integrate via partial fractions to a log expression.
